title: PostgreSQL Logical Decoding and Change Data Capture (CDC) Architecture
realWorldScenario: Your architecture team must stream all real-time changes from `orders`, `payments`, and `customers` to Elasticsearch and Apache Kafka with sub-second latency. A developer proposes using polling queries (`WHERE updated_at > last_poll`).
questionStatement: Critique the polling query anti-pattern for Change Data Capture (CDC). Detail how PostgreSQL Logical Decoding works using Write-Ahead Logs, logical replication slots, and `pgoutput` / Debezium. Explain `REPLICA IDENTITY` (DEFAULT vs FULL) and how hard DELETE events are captured.
expectedConcepts: Shortcomings of polling queries (missed deletes, transaction race conditions, I/O load)
WAL-based logical decoding streaming committed transactions
Logical replication slots and LSN offset tracking
REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT (PK only) vs FULL (complete old row)
hints: Can a polling query detect hard DELETE statements without soft-delete flags?
Where does PostgreSQL write all committed transactions before modifying disk pages?
What does REPLICA IDENTITY FULL record in WAL during an UPDATE?
